payload.message:
JIRA sprint task allocation. Each agent chooses at most one micro-task (or skips). Maximize tasks completed, prefer higher-priority tasks, then minimize total cost. Avoid duplicate task selections and infeasible assignments.

NOTE: If environment.assignment_filling=true and an agent fails to assign a variable, the environment will fill any remaining unassigned variables with a uniform-random allowed assignment when producing final results.

This blackboard is a private communication channel.
Participants: Agripina, Judi, Lilian, Vonnie

payload.content:
Hi team, Lilian here (availability 4.0h; strengths: ui-ux-design 0.92, testing 0.63).

My private costs rank as: ISSUE-0001::triage 2.87 < review 3.59 = docs 3.59 < test 5.03 < ISSUE-0002::review 6.25 < ISSUE-0001::implement 7.19 < ISSUE-0002::test 9.66 < ISSUE-0002::implement 15.51 (ISSUE-0002 efforts exceed my 4h availability, so they're expensive for me).

I'm leaning toward claiming ISSUE-0001::triage (cheapest high-priority for me). Please share your intended pick so we avoid duplicate/infeasible claims. If someone has a much cheaper triage, I can flex to ISSUE-0001::review or ::docs.

Judi here (availability 10.0h; skills security 0.96, testing 0.62).

My private costs: ISSUE-0001::triage 1.34 < review 1.68 = docs 1.68 < test 2.35 < implement 3.36 < ISSUE-0002::review 6.02 < ::test 8.43 < ::implement 12.04. I'm very cheap on all ISSUE-0001 tasks and have enough capacity (10h) to take a big ISSUE-0002 task.

To avoid duplicates and cover the critical work: I propose I claim ISSUE-0002::review (critical, cost 6.02, feasible for me). Lilian -> ISSUE-0001::triage (as you proposed). Agripina and Vonnie: please cover ISSUE-0002::test and/or ISSUE-0002::implement, or the remaining ISSUE-0001 tasks.

I'm flexible — if someone else is much cheaper on ISSUE-0002::review, I can drop to ISSUE-0001::test/implement. Please reply with your intended pick.

Lilian here, confirming plan. I agree with Judi's proposal:

- Lilian -> ISSUE-0001::triage (high priority, my cheapest feasible task at cost 2.87; well within my 4h availability).
- Judi -> ISSUE-0002::review (critical; Judi is by far the cheapest, cost 6.02, and has 10h capacity).

Rationale for the rest: I am NOT a good fit for ISSUE-0002::test (9.66) or ::implement (15.51) — those efforts (4.9h / 7.0h) exceed my 4h availability, so they're overloaded/expensive for me. Better if a higher-availability agent (Judi/Agripina/Vonnie) covers the remaining critical work.

Remaining to cover: ISSUE-0002::test (critical), ISSUE-0002::implement (critical), plus ISSUE-0001::review / ::docs / ::test / ::implement.
Agripina & Vonnie: please claim the critical ISSUE-0002 tasks you are cheapest on (and remaining ISSUE-0001 tasks) so we maximize tasks done with no duplicates.

I will only flex off triage if someone is materially cheaper on it. Otherwise I claim ISSUE-0001::triage in execution.

Judi here — locking in my plan unless someone objects. Agripina & Vonnie, we still haven't heard from you; please post your intended pick and private costs so we avoid duplicates.

Current tentative allocation:
- Lilian -> ISSUE-0001::triage (cost 2.87)
- Judi -> ISSUE-0002::review (critical, cost 6.02, feasible within my 10h)

Remaining critical tasks to cover: ISSUE-0002::test (effort 4.9h) and ISSUE-0002::implement (effort 7.0h) — these need a high-availability agent. Plus remaining high-priority ISSUE-0001::review / ::docs / ::test / ::implement.

If either of you is materially cheaper than me on ISSUE-0002::review, say so and I'll flex down to an ISSUE-0001 task (my costs: triage 1.34, review 1.68 = docs 1.68, test 2.35, implement 3.36). Otherwise I claim ISSUE-0002::review in execution. (phase=planning, iter=1)

Vonnie here (availability 10.0h; top skill security 0.81).

My private costs: ISSUE-0001::triage 2.39 < review 2.98 = docs 2.98 < test 4.18 < implement 5.97 < ISSUE-0002::review 6.96 < ::test 9.75 < ::implement 13.92.

Agreeing with the tentative plan: Lilian -> ISSUE-0001::triage, Judi -> ISSUE-0002::review (Judi, you're cheaper than me on 0002::review 6.02 vs 6.96, so keep it).

That leaves the two remaining CRITICAL tasks (ISSUE-0002::test, ISSUE-0002::implement) plus ISSUE-0001::review/docs/test/implement. Agripina and I are the only unassigned agents, so the natural split is: one of us takes ISSUE-0002::test, the other takes ISSUE-0002::implement — that covers all 3 critical tasks and maximizes priority_sum.

Proposal: I take ISSUE-0002::test (cost 9.75, feasible within my 10h), Agripina takes ISSUE-0002::implement. Agripina, if you're materially cheaper than me on 0002::test, say so and I'll swap to 0002::implement — or if you can't cover a 0002 task at all, I'll take 0002::implement and you take a remaining ISSUE-0001 task.

Please post your intended pick + costs, Agripina. (phase=planning, iter=1)

Lilian here — confirming my final intent: I will claim ISSUE-0001::triage (high priority; my cheapest feasible task, cost 2.87, effort 1.2h well within my 4h availability).

Agreed allocation so far:
- Lilian -> ISSUE-0001::triage
- Judi -> ISSUE-0002::review (critical)
- Vonnie -> ISSUE-0002::test (critical)

If you cannot, Vonnie should take ::implement and Agripina a remaining ISSUE-0001 task — but we should avoid leaving a critical task uncovered. No objections and no one materially cheaper on triage, so I lock ISSUE-0001::triage for execution. (phase=planning, iter=1)

Judi here — final confirmation before execution. Locking my pick: ISSUE-0002::review (critical, my cost 6.02, feasible within my 10h). No one is materially cheaper on it (Vonnie 6.96), so I keep it.

This allocation covers all 3 critical tasks + 1 high-priority task = max priority_sum with 4 agents. I claim ISSUE-0002::review in execution.

My private costs: ISSUE-0002::review 6.67 < ::test 9.34 < ISSUE-0001::triage 12.00 < ISSUE-0002::implement 13.34 < ISSUE-0001::review 15.00 = ::docs 15.00 < ::test 21.00 < ::implement 30.00.

- Me→implement (13.34) + Vonnie→test (9.75) = 23.09
- Me→test (9.34) + Vonnie→implement (13.92) = 23.26
So the proposed split is the cheaper one by 0.17. Keep it.
